title: Heterogeneous GPU interop rehearsal notes 2025
summary: Working-run notes for a rehearsal that validated cross-architecture (H100/A100/T4) driver+CUDA+NCCL interactions, terraform hooks for nodepool upgrades, and concrete rollback criteria for private on-prem clusters.
checklist: etcd snapshot uploaded to s3-compatible store and verified
terraform state unlocked and plan dry-run successful
bastion access keys rotated within last 7 days
monitoring scrapes for gpu-exporter and node-exporter enabled for rehearsal namespace
silence non-critical alerts and create temporary alert baseline
node labels for gpu-class applied to staging nodes
topology_notes: staging canary: 3-node heterogeneous pool: 1x H100, 1x A100, 1x T4
nodepools managed by module gpu-nodepool (current staging ref v0.9-beta)
kube-proxy in ipvs mode and containerd runtime (no docker-shim)
workloads: gpu-sanity (short), gpu-stress (1h allreduce), inference-demo pinned by labels
compatibility_matrix: H100 | NVIDIA Driver 545.85 | CUDA 12.2 | NCCL 2.18 | Observed: baseline, passes nvlink multi-pod allreduce
H100 | NVIDIA Driver 535.104 | CUDA 12.1 | NCCL 2.17 | Observed: intermittent allreduce hang under stress (repro 3/10)
A100 | NVIDIA Driver 535.104 | CUDA 11.8 | NCCL 2.14 | Observed: single-GPU stable, multi-GPU bandwidth regression (~10-15%)
T4  | NVIDIA Driver 470.182 | CUDA 11.4 | NCCL 2.7  | Observed: inference OK, no nvlink on T4; not used for inter-node nvlink tests
General note: driver newer than container CUDA minor can require nvidia-container-toolkit >= required version and occasional libcuda symlink fixes
failure_modes: NCCL allreduce hang when driver/container CUDA mismatch -> symptoms: 100% GPU utilization, no egress, kernel UVM faults in dmesg
containerd fails to expose /dev/nvidia* after driver install -> transient fix: restart containerd + run nvidia-modprobe
slow pod start due to outdated nvidia-container-toolkit (<1.12) when using CUDA 12.x images
RDMA/OFED MTU negotiation failure after driver bump causing degraded NVLink over fabric tests
terraform_notes: gpu-nodepool module current staging ref v0.9-beta
add variable: driver_image_tag (string) to control node image for upgrades
add variable: canary_node_count (int) and post_upgrade_hook (string path) for CI integration
pre-hook recommended: preflight-driver-check.sh that boots ephemeral VM/image and runs nvidia-smi + smoke CUDA sample
recommended outputs: node_pool_name, instance_template_id, image_digest for downstream verification

example usage: module "gpu_nodepool" { source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//gpu-nodepool?ref=v0.9-beta" driver_image_tag = var.driver_image_tag post_upgrade_hook = "/opt/tf-hooks/verify-nvidia.sh" }
rehearsal_steps: 1) Create shadow nodepool via terraform with node_image_tag=driver-545-cuda12.2-20251201
2) Taint new nodes (rehearsal=true:NoSchedule) and run gpu-sanity job across all nodes
3) Execute 1-hour gpu-stress allreduce/allgather collection, collect nvlink counters and heap traces
4) Collect telemetry: nvidia-smi dmon, dcgm-exporter, prom queries for gpu_utilization and pod restarts
5) If green, remove taint and migrate a single inference-demo replica to new nodes and observe 24h
6) Run fast-failure smoke test that injects minor driver mismatch to validate alerting
rollback_triggers: >3 critical GPU OOMs across nodes within 1 hour
reproducible NCCL collective hangs in automated job
>1% of inference requests returning gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED during canary
container restarts >1/hour for inference pods after migration
common_fixes_and_notes: After driver upgrade run: sudo nvidia-modprobe -u -c=0 and restart containerd before assuming devices are available
Ensure nvidia-container-toolkit version matches CUDA minor used by images; add toolkit check in preflight
Avoid mixing driver versions in same scheduler bin by labeling node pools to prevent cross-driver migrations
When using RDMA ensure OFED stack compatibility with new driver to avoid MTU and negotiation issues
